summary: Hartness State Airport (VSF) is a small general aviation airport serving North Springfield, Vermont, nestled in the Connecticut River Valley. It is named after James Hartness, a former Vermont Governor (1921–1923), accomplished aviator, and prolific inventor who held numerous patents in aviation instrumentation. The airport primarily supports recreational flying, flight training, and private aircraft operations in the southeastern Vermont region.
faqs:
Q: What is Hartness State Airport primarily used for?
A: It serves general aviation activities including private flying, flight instruction, and recreational aircraft operations, with no scheduled commercial service.

Q: Who was the airport named after?
A: The airport honors James Hartness, a Vermont Governor from 1921 to 1923, who was also a renowned aviation pioneer, mechanical engineer, and holder of multiple aviation-related patents.

Q: How many runways does the airport have?
A: Hartness State Airport features a single asphalt runway designated 5/23.

Q: Are there any nearby airports?
A: Yes, nearby facilities include Lebanon Municipal Airport (LEB) in New Hampshire and Rutland Southern Vermont Regional Airport (RUT), both offering additional general aviation services.
transport_tips: Ground transportation options are limited, so arranging a rental car or pre-booked ride in advance is strongly recommended. The airport is conveniently located near Interstate 91, making it an easy drive from Brattleboro, White River Junction, or the Keene, New Hampshire area. On-site parking is typically available adjacent to the terminal for pilots and visitors.
local_tip: If you're flying in for a visit, consider scheduling your trip around fall foliage season—late September through mid-October—when the Connecticut River Valley surrounding the airport offers some of the most spectacular autumn color in New England, easily accessible from the field.
